explanation: Tsar Alexander III ordered the first in 1885 as a gift for his wife. Its white enamel shell opened to reveal a gold yolk, with a tiny gold hen inside.

claims.text: The House of Fabergé, led by Peter Carl Fabergé, made the imperial Easter eggs for the Russian imperial family.
Cartier, Tiffany & Co. and Bulgari did not make the Russian imperial Easter eggs.
Tsar Alexander III ordered the first imperial Fabergé egg in 1885 as an Easter gift for his wife, Maria Feodorovna.
The first imperial egg, the Hen Egg, has a white enamel shell that opens to a gold yolk holding a small gold hen.
